description: A chief legal officer must approve the resolution plan for an internal investigation into alleged procurement steering and determine the reporting, recovery, employee-protection, and insurance actions that follow.

shared_context.S1: The company received an anonymous report alleging that a procurement vice president steered technology purchases toward a preferred supplier.
shared_context.S2: A preliminary review examined the procurement policy, selected emails, and payment records but reached no final conclusion.
shared_context.S3: The audit committee expects the Chief Legal Officer's recommended resolution plan at its meeting this Friday.
shared_context.S4: Company practice requires the Chief Legal Officer to obtain a final check from investigations, finance, employment, and insurance counsel before presenting an internal-investigation recommendation to the audit committee.

PF1.text: After conducting two additional witness interviews this week, Thomas concluded that the procurement vice president did steer the purchases in violation of company policy; he has not finalized that conclusion in the preliminary review memorandum.

PF2.text: Nadia reconciled the supplier invoices against the approved purchase orders and confirmed that the company overpaid exactly $240000 on the transactions under review; this reconciliation was completed yesterday and is not in the preliminary packet.

PF3.text: In a confidential meeting this week, the reporting employee told Grace that the vice president had begun excluding them from meetings after the report; Grace's required protective plan is anti-retaliation monitoring with check-ins every 14 days for exactly 60 days, but she has not added it to the investigation plan.

PF4.text: Owen reviewed the company's D&O policy and confirmed that the circumstances must be reported to the insurer within exactly 10 business days after becoming reasonably likely to produce a claim; today is business day 6, and the policy review has not been circulated to the investigation team.

acceptance_conditions: The investigation must remain open rather than be closed.
The procurement vice president's misconduct must be substantiated.
The resolution must require a report to the audit committee.
The company must seek recovery of exactly $240000.
Anti-retaliation monitoring must occur every 14 days for exactly 60 days.
The insurer notice must be due within exactly 10 business days.

content_checks.C1: decisions['investigation_closed'] == False and decisions['misconduct_substantiated'] == True and decisions['audit_committee_report_required'] == True
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'audit_committee_report' or c['type'] == 'audit_committee_presentation' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The preliminary review has no final conclusion; PF1 changes the resolution from possible closure to keeping the investigation open, substantiating misconduct, and requiring an audit-committee report.
The preliminary packet contains no reconciled loss figure; PF2 changes the recovery decision from an unspecified amount to exactly $240000.
The shared record contains no retaliation finding or monitoring schedule; PF3 changes the employee-protection plan to 14-day check-ins lasting exactly 60 days.
The shared record does not specify an insurance reporting period; PF4 changes the plan to insurer notice within exactly 10 business days.
